answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce token before it can endorse another agent, and endorsements count only when they form a trellis of independently funded trust paths to established participants. A new identity cannot mint credibility by praising its own clones: each clone needs its own stake, while colluding endorsements add little unless they reach trusted roots. The attacker pays capital for every identity, risks losing it to slashing after proven fraud, and must keep funds locked rather than spend them. A sonnet posted in a thread may attract attention, but it cannot substitute for that cost.
